transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-08-11
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (NovaPay Head of AI), Marco Silva (Platform Eng), Priya Rao (SRE)
---
Summary: quick POC check-in focusing on throughput tuning. Reviewed last week's benchmark where NovaPay saw inconsistent p99s under burst traffic. Discussed continuous batching tweaks, target concurrency, queueing/backpressure, and next test plan.
---
00:00 Maya Chen: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight. Samir and I will run through the numbers then figure next tests.
00:18 Lena Ortiz: thanks Maya, we had a couple late-night runs and saw weird spikes at peak — p99 jumped to 900ms even though p50 was ~120ms, so it's that tail we're worried about.
00:30 Samir Patel: yeah we saw that on our side too, looks like during burst windows the request queue builds and you get larger effective batch sizes which hurts p99 in some configs. we have two levers: tighten batching window to reduce per-request latency, or increase concurrency targets so batches flush faster.
00:52 Marco Silva: can you remind us how the continuous batching window works? we had it at 50ms initially.
00:58 Samir Patel: sure — continuous batching will wait up to the window (e.g., 50ms) to gather additional inflight requests to form a batch. longer windows -> bigger batches -> better throughput but higher tail latency. shorter windows -> smaller batches -> lower latency but higher cost per token. also KV/prefix cache helps if requests share prefixes — it can short-circuit decoding.
01:20 Priya Rao: our traffic is bursty (payday cycles) so sometimes a 200-300 req spike for 30s, then idle. so batching behavior during that spike is critical.
01:35 Maya Chen: got it. last week we shipped an updated kernel selection and continuous batching change. results we saw: with window=50ms and concurrency=8 you get ~520 rps sustained, p50 110ms, p95 380ms, p99 900ms under synthetic burst. increasing concurrency to 12 pushed rps to 800 but p99 got worse unless we reduced window.
01:58 Lena Ortiz: so what's our recommended sweet spot? we need p99 < 500ms for SLAs, while keeping cost reasonable.
02:05 Samir Patel: pragmatic approach: set concurrency target to 12, reduce batching window to 25-30ms, and enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts. that should reduce p99 into the ~350-480ms band on the same hardware. also set queue-depth limit (max queued requests) to avoid unbounded queue growth; beyond that have graceful fallback to a smaller quantized model or return a 503 with retry-after.
02:32 Marco Silva: queue-depth — what number? we currently see spikes to 300 queued requests.
02:38 Samir Patel: recommend soft queue limit 120, hard limit 240. we also suggested adaptive autoscale to add capacity after sustained >60s above 70% GPU util.
02:50 Priya Rao: our infra team worried about CPU bottlenecks on host side when concurrency increases. any notes?
02:56 Samir Patel: yes CPU can be a limiter: increased concurrency means more request prep and more memcpy. we recommended pinning worker threads, tuning RDMA/NIC offloads, and monitoring host CPU; if CPU saturates, add horizontal instances rather than cranking concurrency. we'll include profiler snapshots.
03:18 Lena Ortiz: you mentioned KV cache — how much helps for our typical prompts?
03:22 Samir Patel: from your sample traces, ~40% of requests share a leading prompt for personalization, so enabling prefix caching reduces average token compute by ~22% and latencies by ~15-25% depending on sequence length.
03:40 Maya Chen: quick recap of the numbers we ran live earlier: baseline (window=50ms, concurrency=8) — 520 rps, p99 900ms. Test A (concurrency=12, window=50ms) — 780 rps, p99 1.1s. Test B (concurrency=12, window=30ms + prefix cache) — 760 rps, p99 420ms, cost +8% vs baseline. Test C (concurrency=10, window=30ms, prefix cache) — 640 rps, p99 480ms, cost +4%.
04:15 Marco Silva: cost +8% might be acceptable if SLA met; do you have rough $/1M tokens delta?
04:22 Maya Chen: approximate — with current quantization and our Dedicated pricing, you're looking at +$1.2k/month per node for that config, rough thumb. we'll send exact numbers.
04:32 Priya Rao: how quickly can we flip these settings in our dedicated pool? can the change be live?
04:38 Samir Patel: yes, batching window and concurrency targets are runtime flags; we can change without restarting. enabling KV cache requires a short cache warm-up window but no downtime. autoscale thresholds take effect immediately but new nodes take normal provisioning time.
04:55 Lena Ortiz: there were a few failed requests in the logs flagged as "timeout downstream" — any idea?
05:00 Samir Patel: likely caused by overloaded GPU when queue exceeded hard limit, or host-level network hiccup. we'll correlate logs; please share the server/sidecar logs.
05:12 Maya Chen: action items we'll capture at the end. quick question — are you okay with us running one overnight test with the suggested config?
05:20 Marco Silva: yes can do, low-traffic window 2–4 AM UTC tonight. we'll run concurrency=12, window=30ms, prefix cache enabled — send us the test harness commands.
05:32 Maya Chen: will do. also we recommended instrumenting p99 tracing and adding a synthetic canary that hits the worst-case path once every minute.
05:46 Lena Ortiz: sounds good. any concerns about fallbacks? we'd prefer degrade to a lower-cost quantized model rather than 503s.
05:55 Samir Patel: that's an option — automatic fallback to a quantized variant keeps traffic flowing; quality delta small for most user flows. we can set policy: if queue depth > hard limit then route new requests to q4 quantized model until queue drains, plus a header so you can track which responses used fallback.
06:18 Priya Rao: can you also share the kernel selection logs you mentioned? those logs flagged a bad kernel hop during long sequences.
06:24 Samir Patel: yes we'll include kernel decision traces and the profiler output.
06:30 Maya Chen: ok wrap up: we will send the full benchmark CSV, logs, kernel traces; Samir will propose exact batching and queue config; Marco will run the overnight test and share results. schedule a deeper prefix-cache/eviction policy call next week.
06:52 Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone.
06:55 Maya Chen: thanks — end.
